summary: Harold C. Conklin was an anthropologist and linguist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley (1943–1950) and Yale (Ph.D. ~1950–1955). He held posts at Columbia (1955), Yale (1962–1996), and the Peabody Museum of Natural History (1974–1996).

Harold Edward Musson was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Wellington College, St Edmund's School, and Magdalene College, Cambridge (BA 1938), he studied under traditional teachers Pelene Siri Vajiragnana and Nyanatiloka Mahathera, serving earlier in the British military.

Harold G. Coward is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who completed his doctorate in philosophy at McMaster University (1973). He served as a professor and press director at the University of Calgary and directed at the University of Victoria.

Harold Hargreaves worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Formerly headmaster of Government High School, Amritsar, he served extensively with the Archaeological Survey of India as Superintendent and Deputy Director General between 1910 and 1931.

Harold Herman Bender was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian studies. He studied at Lafayette College, Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, and Berlin under Richard Pischel and Wilhelm Schulze, later serving at Princeton University from 1909 to 1950.

Harold Scheub studied at the University of Michigan, UCLA, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD ~1965–1969). After teaching at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School, he spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2013).
Harold Stewart was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music and the University of Sydney (~1938–1939).

Harold Walter Bailey worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at the University of Western Australia and Oxford under F. W. Thomas and R. P. Dewhurst, he taught at SOAS (1929–1936) and Cambridge (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani was an Indologist and historian who studied at Aligarh Muslim University, Oxford, and under Ghulam Yazdani. He held academic posts at Osmania University (~1919–1945), Nizam College (~1945–1948), and Zakir Husain Delhi College (~1948–1951).

Harry Campbell Norman was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Edinburgh under Samuel Henry Butcher, William Ross Hardie, and Julius Eggeling, and at Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell, later teaching at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Harry Charles Purvis Bell worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Cheltenham College in 1864 and joined the Ceylon Civil Service in 1873.

Harry Falk is a scholar of Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Ulrich Schneider and Gaya Charan Tripathi. He served at the University of Freiburg (~1976–1993), Ruhr University Bochum, and the Free University of Berlin (1993–2012).

Harry Halén is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies. He studied under Pentti Aalto (~1965–1974) and served as an amanuensis at the University of Helsinki from approximately 1970 to 2008.
Harsha Dehejia is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who was educated at the University of Mumbai and became Professor of Hindu Studies at Carleton University around 1994.

Harsha Gautam is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Texas at Austin (PhD 2021). She held posts at UT Austin and the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

Harshit Mishra works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Delhi, the International School for Jain Studies, Central Sanskrit University, and Ghent University, and worked as a research associate at the International School for Jain Studies in 2024.

Hartmut Buescher is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhal Tripathi. He held positions at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.

Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Friedrich Weller and completed his doctorate under Paul Thieme. He later served as Professor Emeritus at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel was an Indologist who studied under Paul Thieme. He held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and edited the Verzeichnis der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland.

Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Gakushuin University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Nagasaki University from approximately 1980 to 2004.
